candidates: When adding or updating GitHub repository links in documentation, verify that each URL actually resolves before merging: check that subdirectory paths within the monorepo are correct (package locations can move between releases), and use `/tree/` rather than `/blob/` when the link target is a directory rather than a file.

In Markdown documentation files, never use bare URLs (violates MD034); wrap standalone URLs in angle brackets (e.g., `<https://example.com>`) or embed them in named links (e.g., `[descriptive text](https://example.com)`).

When updating documentation to list a narrowed set of recommended framework or package options (e.g., reducing a list of supported build-tool variants), explicitly state whether the omitted options are deprecated-but-still-available or fully removed, so users with legacy or special build requirements are not misled into thinking those options no longer exist.

When a code example introduces an import from a package or API surface that was added in a specific version (e.g., `defineConfig`/`globalIgnores` from `eslint/config` requiring ESLint v9.22.0+), document the minimum version required inline and, where the project officially supports older versions of that dependency, provide an alternative import path (e.g., `@eslint/config-helpers`) or a clearly visible callout for users on those older versions.
